before: while checks its condition before each repetition. If it is false at the start, no repetition happens.
< means strictly less than. $count < 3 is false once count equals 3.
A counter is a value used to track repetitions. Updating it inside this loop eventually makes the condition false.
This loop prints the current counter, then adds one. The stopping value itself does not print.
Expected result: 0, 1, 2 on separate lines. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A loop repeats instructions while its test is true.
The first value is zero. Each turn prints the current count before adding one.
Only counts below three get a turn.
The output is `0`, then `1`, then `2`. Three is the first value that fails the test.
